next_round_constraints: Prioritize templates with an explicit hospitalization state and direct observation of H (or a closely related hospitalization flow), rather than delayed_I-only observation maps.
If using delays, keep delay_weeks in a narrow neighborhood around 0–1; avoid exploring larger delays unless paired with an explicit H compartment.
Prefer simpler observation maps aligned to the target (H-only) over composite maps (e.g., I+H) unless there is a clear mechanistic justification.
Control instability: when adding extra compartments (e.g., SEIRS), require configurations that do not increase rolling variability; favor structures that remain stable across rolling splits.
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity: SEIR with delayed_I at 2 weeks shows much worse single validation behavior than 1 week, suggesting the template is brittle to delay choice and may be misaligned with the hospitalization-rate observation process.

Observation mismatch: SEIR/SEIRS using delayed_I underperforms relative to models that include an explicit hospitalization compartment observed as H, indicating that mapping hospitalizations directly from infectious prevalence is likely misspecified for this series.

Peak handling instability: SEIRS improves rolling mean error but has notably higher rolling variability, consistent with difficulty stabilizing around sharp peaks (high peakiness) when adding waning-immunity dynamics.

Over-mixing signals: SEIHR with I+H observation is worse than observing H alone, suggesting that combining incidence-like and hospitalization-like signals in the observation map can dilute the hospitalization-rate target signal.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For the next round, focus proposals on hospitalization-explicit structures (e.g., SEIHR-family) with observation_map set to H (or hospitalization flow if available) and delay_weeks=0 or 1. De-emphasize SEIR/SEIRS with delayed_I as the sole observation. Avoid composite observation maps like I+H unless you can justify why it should track hospitalization rate better than H alone. If exploring immunity-waning extensions, constrain them to variants that preserve rolling stability (do not broaden the search to many added dynamics at once).
